cost_ledger_annotations.text: Summer 1992: Herceg-Bosna's institutions formalized on the 3 July statute; the HVO declared its supreme defence body. An institutional fact for the political map to come.
July 1992: local HVO consolidation over the Kaonik/Novi Travnik/Ljuta arms sites allowed to stand; the joint anti-VRS front frays through dispute, short of open war.
Summer 1992: the HVO deepened its dependence on Zagreb's two-track arming and officer-secondment channel (Susak/Tudjman); better-supplied, but more tightly bound to Zagreb's agenda.
RBiH-HRHB cooperation drifted below 0.40 with measurable recent erosion; ceiling-locked for 30 turns.

Displacement reckoning surface. Triggered when cumulative inbound displacement to RBiH-controlled municipalities crosses 100,000 persons. The historical reference set: the Research and Documentation Centre Sarajevo (RDC) Bosnian Book of Dead and the UNHCR figures cited at Prosecutor v. Krajišnik (IT-00-39-T, 27 September 2006, paras. 706-727) document approximately 2.2 million displaced persons across the 1992-1995 conflict, of whom roughly 1.2 million were internally displaced inside Bosnia and Herzegovina, with the largest single waves originating from the 1992 ethnic-cleansing campaigns in eastern Bosnia, the Drina valley, and the Prijedor / Sanski Most area (ICTY findings of crimes against humanity and persecution at Krajišnik paras. 1080-1117 and Prosecutor v. Stakić IT-97-24-T paras. 700-716). This annotation registers the reception-side strain — supply degradation and cohesion erosion in absorbing municipalities — as the documentary counterpart to the displacement record. Civilian-protection legal standard: Geneva Convention IV Article 49.

Audit-only origin-tracing ledger. When the displaced-in origin OSID set intersects an enclave municipality, the joint observation (origin: enclave; destination: RBiH-government area) is recorded for Dayton-scoring narrative. The ledger does not flip rupture wiring or enclave_resilience aggregates; it ensures the endgame reckoning can describe the demographic flow truthfully — which enclaves emptied where, on which trajectory, and across which turn window. ICTY Prosecutor v. Krstić (IT-98-33-T, paras. 153-179) is the canonical reference for the Srebrenica enclave-emptying flow; this annotation is the engine-internal documentary record of analogous flows within run-state.

RBiH civic identity consolidated after the founding choice. Cohesion +3 and recruitment +4% for 28 turns reflect minority-cadre retention and diplomatic legitimacy, not a claim that civic politics erased wartime coercion or suffering.
Refugee labor mobilization activated under displaced-in>80000 and refugee_absorption_strain. Recruitment +8% for 25 turns; cohesion -2 to reflect institutional cost.
